rationale: Fix the startup-recovery selection obligation and execute it in one product. Source reading supports the responsibility without presuming a violation: NewRaft's restoreSnapshot tries the listed snapshots in order and keeps the first that loads, so startup recovery is entitled to rely on the SnapshotStore contract that List returns the highest index first; the same in-repository comparator that breaks that contract therefore decides which state a restarting node adopts. The direct check seeds two real snapshots in inverse (term, index) order, starts a real Raft on an empty log so recovery must come from a snapshot, and compares the adopted applied index with the highest retained index. Construction in a scratch copy of the captured source showed the node adopting index 50 while the store retained index 80; that local run is construction knowledge only and formal evidence requires the trusted runner's clean-copy execution, which is requested here.

candidate.rationale: Recorded as a new sourced question anchored on the same principal Fact from its consumption side: the ordering fact is what the startup recovery selects by, and the recovery duty is that the adopted baseline must be the most advanced retained state. The claim is bounded to the in-repository store and the constructed retention, excludes the leader's send path and the later scan consequence, and is offered as ready_for_check.

obligation.description: NewRaft's startup recovery must adopt the retained snapshot with the highest applied index, so that a restart does not set its applied baseline below the most advanced state the snapshot store holds; a consumer that takes the first listed snapshot must therefore be given the highest-index one.

scope.description: A node starting with an empty log and stable store and a FileSnapshotStore retaining two snapshots whose terms and indexes are ordered in opposite directions, so the restore path must choose between them.
assumptions: Both snapshots are readable and load successfully, so the choice is decided by the order alone.
The node has no log or stable state that could pin its applied baseline independently.
excluded: The leader's snapshot send path, which is a different consumer of the same order
The later configuration-scan behaviour when a hole lies above the adopted snapshot
Snapshot stores supplied by callers that do not implement this ordering

parameters.selection_rule: restoreSnapshot keeps the first listed snapshot that loads

pending: A startup scenario over an inversely ordered retained pair that reports the adopted applied index against the highest retained index.

grounding.derivation: restoreSnapshot lists the snapshots, tries them in order and, on the first success, sets lastApplied and lastSnapshot from that snapshot, so the first listed entry determines the recovered baseline. The interface states the list is ordered with the highest index first, and the in-repository comparator orders by term first, so a recovery that follows the list inherits that ordering's choice.
grounding.applicability: Applies to the startup recovery of the in-repository store under the constructed inverse retention; it asserts no obligation for the send path or for stores with conformant ordering.
unresolved: Whether a running node retains an inversely ordered pair.
Whether the later configuration scan would then fail on a hole.
alternatives: If the store listed the highest index first, recovery would adopt it and this duty would be met.

bindings.description: The loop in restoreSnapshot that tries the listed snapshots in order and, on the first success, sets lastApplied and lastSnapshot from that snapshot's index and term.
pending: Whether a later snapshot in the list could be preferred by any other rule.

associations.rationale: This loop is what turns the list order into the node's recovered applied baseline, so it is the code that must receive the highest-index snapshot first.

question.question: When a node restarts with an empty log and a snapshot store retaining two snapshots whose (term, index) positions are inversely ordered, does startup recovery adopt the snapshot with the highest applied index - the state the store actually holds most recently - or does it adopt the lower-index snapshot because the first listed entry is chosen by term order, leaving the node's applied baseline below what the store holds?
question.importance: Startup recovery sets the node's applied baseline, which decides which entries are replayed and which state the FSM is restored to. Adopting a lower-index snapshot regresses the node's state relative to its own store until a leader re-supplies the missing range, so the concern is a recovery/state-selection duty; the same order also decides which snapshot a leader ships to a lagging follower.
question.trigger_rationale: The recovery path trusts the store's documented ordering and takes the first entry that loads, while the in-repository comparator orders by term first. The two statements only diverge for inversely ordered retention, a store state the code neither prevents nor checks, so the selection has to be observed with such a pair rather than assumed from the comparator alone.

supporting_behavior_ids.B-snapshot-install: Context: the other consumer of the same ordering is the leader's sendLatestSnapshot, which also selects the first listed snapshot to ship to a lagging follower; the two consumers share the ordering duty.

contexts: Node startup with an empty log and stable store and a FileSnapshotStore retaining an inversely ordered pair
Recovery attempting the listed snapshots in order
Later replication that must re-supply entries above the adopted baseline if it is too low
event_paths: restoreSnapshot iterates the list; the first snapshot whose Open and FSM restore succeed is adopted
adopted snapshot -> setLastApplied(snapshot.Index), setLastSnapshot(snapshot.Index, snapshot.Term), configuration from the snapshot
NewRaft configuration scan from the adopted index to the last log index
leader appendEntries/snapshot install re-supplies entries above the adopted baseline
counterevidence: restoreSnapshot falls through to the next listed snapshot when one fails to load, so a bad first choice does not necessarily prevent startup
A conformant store would list the highest index first and the recovery would adopt it, so the duty is met whenever the store honours the interface
Snapshots taken from one node's own log have terms and indexes ordered together, so the divergence requires the inverse pair rather than ordinary retention
The adopted snapshot is the node's own store content either way, so no state outside the node is discarded by the choice itself
unknowns: Whether a node can retain an inversely ordered pair in a legal history, for example an older local snapshot with a high last-entry term beside a snapshot installed from a leader whose last entry has a lower term but a higher index
Whether the startup configuration scan would then panic on a hole above the adopted baseline, which is a separate consequence not part of this duty
Whether callers expect recovery to prefer the highest applied index or the highest-term snapshot, which would decide whether the interface comment or the comparator is the normative statement
